caption: I've never added up the small deposits until now. Have you ever checked yours?

slides.title:
The R3 400 I don't
tell anyone about,
on R18 300 p/m
South Africa
Living in Ga-Rankuwa
slides.body:
Male, 27
Single, no kids
Job: Laboratory technician at a provincial hospital
Net salary: R18 300 p/m

slides.title: Betting
slides.includes: Sports betting app deposits, mostly weekends
slides.body: Deposits, not losses. I won some back, which I know isn't how the arithmetic works.

slides.title: Rent
slides.includes: Backroom with its own entrance, water included
slides.body: Cheap, quiet, and my landlady waves when I come home late.

slides.title: Groceries
slides.includes: Cooking for one, bulk buying maize meal and chicken
slides.body: The most disciplined line on this list, strangely.

slides.title: Taxi fare
slides.includes: Ga-Rankuwa to the hospital, back late after shifts
slides.body: Night shift means no taxi after 9 and an e-hailing ride home.

slides.title: Family support
slides.includes: My mom's electricity and my sister's data
slides.body: Betting is more than I send home. I noticed that on my statement.

slides.title: Everything else
slides.includes: Phone contract, clothing account, funeral policy, stokvel, haircuts, airtime
slides.body: Nothing in here surprises me. That's the problem: the other line does.

slides.title: What's left
slides.body: Out of R18 300. About R57 a day, and the betting line is bigger than my rent.

slides.title: I stopped guessing
slides.body:
I uploaded my statement to Beyond Horizon and the recurring deposits showed up grouped together.

Seeing them as one number was different to seeing them as small ones.

No bank login needed.
